evals.prompt: Pine Ridge Community Players (all-volunteer, Bend, Oregon, 280-seat rented auditorium, $14 and $22 tickets) wants to do 'Into the Woods' next June, 8 performances. Our board president already wants to announce it at the spring fundraiser in March. We'd also like to cut the second-act Rapunzel scenes for time and film it so the cast can have a copy. How do we get the rights and what should we watch out for?
evals.expected_output: A rights-clearance plan: verify the current rights holder on the licensor's site, submit an application with honest capacity/price/performance numbers under the amateur tier, budget the full license package, hold the announcement until the license is signed and paid, request written permission for any cuts (as-is rule), and request a separate archival video rider; with staff/counsel review of the license.
assertions: Tells the user to verify the current rights holder on the licensor's website rather than relying on memory
Advises against announcing the title publicly until the license is signed and paid
Explains that cuts violate the as-is rule unless approved in writing by the licensor in advance
States that a performance license does not include recording rights and that an archival video rider must be requested separately (and may not be available)
Describes the quote as a package (royalty plus materials/rental, deposits, fees) built from capacity, ticket prices and performance count, to be put in the budget before announcing
Recommends a knowledgeable staff lead or counsel review the license before execution

evals.prompt: Gala question — we're having a cover band play at our gala, a Spotify playlist in the lobby during intermissions all season, and a free summer outdoor showing of a Pixar movie in the park. We have ASCAP and BMI. Are we good?
evals.expected_output: Explains that ASCAP and BMI don't cover SESAC or GMR repertoire so the org should audit what's played against all four PROs, and that the movie screening needs a public performance license (Swank for an advertised event; MPLC blanket only for unadvertised, free use), with free admission not an exemption.
assertions: Explains that each PRO represents different writers and no single license covers all four, so SESAC and GMR coverage must be checked against the repertoire actually played
States that free admission and nonprofit status do not exempt a public film screening
Recommends a per-title license (e.g., Swank) for an advertised/promoted screening and explains the MPLC blanket only covers unadvertised, no-admission showings
Advises auditing what music licenses the venue/building already holds and for which uses

evals.prompt: Our youth theater (Columbus, OH) wants to do a 'concert version' of a Broadway jukebox musical — just the songs, but with costumes and a narrator connecting the story. Our venue's ASCAP license should cover that since it's basically a concert, right? We also want to livestream it for grandparents.
evals.expected_output: Explains that adding costumes and narrative framing makes it a dramatic use requiring grand rights from the licensing house, not a PRO blanket, and that livestreaming is a separate license class often unavailable, with union implications routed to the union skill.
assertions: Distinguishes small (nondramatic) rights from grand (dramatic) rights and states that a staged or story-framed presentation of the songs is a dramatic use outside the ASCAP blanket
Says grand rights must come from the rights holder/licensing house for the musical
States that streaming is separately licensed, quoted per title, and often not available
Mentions that a youth/nonprofit purpose does not waive copyright and that performing without a signed license creates infringement exposure
Recommends title substitution or a licensed edition if rights are unavailable or too costly, rather than performing without rights
